d_eff_adjustments: Quansah suspension (ENG straight red vs Mexico, auto 1-match ban; treat OUT pending FA appeal): -10 ENG. CB depth loss + forces RB reshuffle with Reece James also a hamstring doubt. Modest because first-choice CB pair Stones+Guehi remain and RB cover is deep (Walker/Konsa/Spence).
Moller Wolfe (NOR starting LB) fitness doubt after knock vs Brazil: -4 NOR (half-weight of a full LB downgrade, he may still play).

England harder R16 (36 min with 10 men, Azteca altitude + longer international trip to Miami): -2 ENG net, offset by ~5-6 days rest, altitude-drop recovery benefit, and Miami heat/humidity hitting both sides.
inputs.venue: Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens FL (neutral; neither team is a host) -> no +75 host bonus
inputs.pk_note: Kept default 0.5. Considered a small England shootout edge (Pickford's documented PK-save record, England's improved recent shootout history) but held conservative to avoid overfitting a single-datapoint keeper adjustment; England lean noted, not priced in.

payload.rationale: M is calibrated Elo->1x2 (predict_1x2, neutral symmetrized) at d_eff=-96. England is a genuine top-4 side (Elo #4, elite defensive xG ~0.58/game) vs Norway (Elo #8 but on a large recent surge; first-ever WC QF). Norway's R16 win over Brazil massively flattered their process (0.84 xG vs Brazil 2.73) - a pure Haaland finishing/keeper heist; England's R16 win over Mexico also flattered process (out-xG'd, won a man down on finishing + game-state). Net: England clear but not overwhelming favorite (47.3%), live draw (29.0%), Norway 23.7%. J = M: no market-unavailable information exists to justify deviating. All material facts (Quansah suspension, injuries, Haaland's quality) are public and priced. Haaland's finishing premium is real but SYMMETRIC (England's Kane +2.37 over xG, Bellingham also overperform) so it ~cancels in the 1x2, and is constrained by Norway's weak chance creation vs England's elite defense. The loud 'Norway is Elo-inflated / R16 was variance' signal is the doctrine-forbidden 'Elo overrates' input (would make J a market simulator - the m91/Rui-Alg lesson); it is explanation-only and NOT fed to J.
invalidation: Quansah suspension overturned on FA appeal AND he starts -> remove the -10 ENG adjustment (amend toward England).
Confirmed pre-match XI shows Norway missing Odegaard OR Haaland (injury, not rotation) -> large amend toward England.
Confirmed pre-match XI shows England resting/missing multiple first-choice starters (Kane/Bellingham/Rice) -> amend toward Norway.
Moller Wolfe confirmed OUT and replaced by a clear downgrade -> extend the -4 NOR adjustment.
Extreme weather / lightning delay materially altering the game -> note but do not repredict.

basis: J = M by deliberate discipline. Consulted the full evidence pack (Opta tournament-win, Dimers 54.1% England, xG both teams, Haaland/Kane/Bellingham finishing data, unanimous expert previews favoring England).
No LEGITIMATE market-unavailable information found to move J off M: Quansah suspension, all injuries, and Haaland's finishing quality are public and priced by sharp books.

Haaland 'finisher premium' (a permitted J input per revised protocol) was weighed but NOT applied net, because it is symmetric with England's own overperforming finishers (Kane +2.37/xG, Bellingham) and is throttled by Norway's weak chance creation (0.84 xG vs Brazil) against England's elite defense (~0.58 xGA/game) -> no clean directional 1x2 edge.

Rejected input (doctrine): 'Norway's Elo is inflated by a recent surge and their R16 was variance.' This is the forbidden 'Elo-vs-market known divergence' mechanism; it would turn J into a market simulator (m91/Rui-Alg lesson). Explanation-only: it predicts the market may price Norway at or below M's 23.7%, but J does not move on it.

Expected M/J-vs-market posture: if market prices Norway <= ~23.7% (England >= ~47%, likely toward Dimers' 54%), any Norway-side gap is my model's inflation bias, not a market error -> Pass per m95 discipline. Committed to J=M as a real, scorable data point.
